headline: US: 10-year Treasury yield climbs to 5% for the first time since 2023

evidence.dominant_driver: US10Y briefly breaking 5% as oil-driven inflation and Fed-hike expectations lift long-term discount rates

market_expectations.distribution_notes: Contemporaneous reports placed a quarter-point hike probability near 87-89%.

absorption.reason: US10Y briefly reached roughly 5.01% but retreated near 4.96% by decision time; equities also recovered part of their initial losses.

observed_reaction.oil_pullback_note: WTI and Brent had pulled back materially from intraday highs while remaining elevated.

observations.DXY: firmer near 99.60, bearish for gold and long-duration equities
observations.US2Y: elevated around 4.65%, consistent with tighter policy expectations
observations.US10Y: rejected the 5% area and eased near 4.96%, reducing immediate pressure
observations.VIX: elevated versus prior sessions but not showing a fresh panic spike at decision time
observations.WTI: around 100.96 after pulling back from above 104
observations.BRENT: around 105.46 after pulling back from near 110
observations.equities: major US indices remained softer but had recovered part of the initial decline

evidence.decision_notes: Forecast targets residual movement from decision time, not the already-observed initial reaction to the 5% threshold.

immediate.rationale: The 5% yield shock has faded from its peak, limiting a fresh directional impulse.

next_session.rationale: Rates remain restrictive, but the rejection of 5% reduces confidence in immediate continuation.

15m.rationale: Residual move is unclear after US10Y backed away from 5%.

1h.rationale: High yields cap upside but partial reversal in rates argues against chasing downside.

4h.rationale: Persistently high discount rates can reassert pressure on long-duration tech if yields stabilize near current levels.

next_session.rationale: Fed expectations remain restrictive, but much of the threshold shock is already absorbed.

predictions.mechanism: Long-duration tech is highly sensitive to discount-rate changes around the 5% US10Y threshold.
predictions.invalidation: A sustained US10Y break back above 5.01% with renewed VIX acceleration would strengthen the bearish case; a drop toward 4.90% would weaken it.
predictions.counter_case: Dip-buying and a continued retreat in yields could produce a relief rebound despite still-high absolute rates.

immediate.rationale: The rate shock is material but no longer intensifying at decision time.

next_session.rationale: High yields remain a valuation headwind while fading oil and yield extremes temper continuation risk.

15m.rationale: US10Y rejected 5%, creating two-sided residual risk.

1h.rationale: Valuation pressure persists but is offset by the retreat in yields and oil from intraday highs.

4h.rationale: If yields remain near 5%, broader equity valuation pressure can re-emerge.

next_session.rationale: The next move depends more on whether 5% becomes sustained than on the already-seen threshold touch.

predictions.mechanism: A near-5% risk-free yield raises the equity discount rate and competes with stocks for capital.
predictions.invalidation: A decisive yield retreat and easing Fed-hike pricing would remove the main bearish driver.
predictions.counter_case: The 5% rejection may mark a near-term rates peak and support a broad relief rally.

immediate.rationale: Gold already sold off sharply and the yield spike has partially reversed.

next_session.rationale: Dollar and yields remain headwinds but geopolitical demand and oversold conditions create offsetting forces.

15m.rationale: A large prior decline plus falling yields from the peak makes further immediate downside less clean.

1h.rationale: Firm DXY conflicts with the pullback in US10Y from 5%.

4h.rationale: Rates remain bearish for gold, but safe-haven demand and prior absorption limit conviction.

next_session.rationale: Direction depends on whether yields re-break 5% or continue retreating.

predictions.mechanism: Higher yields and a stronger dollar raise the opportunity cost of holding gold, but geopolitical risk offsets part of that pressure.
predictions.invalidation: A renewed US10Y breakout above 5% with DXY strength would turn the setup more bearish; a sharp yield decline would favor gold recovery.
predictions.counter_case: Geopolitical safe-haven demand could overpower the rates channel if Middle East tensions worsen again.
